headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad network/API and secret-handling can amplify data leakage and cascading errors when paired with the non-runnable data-engineering course, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict are limited by the course’s…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: The pair has no documented shared runtime channel: agent_a is non-runnable and exposes no io_surfaces, while agent_b is a runnable crawler with MCP/API surfaces. That makes direct injection unlikely, but if outputs are manually copied into Firecrawl prompts or scrape inputs, web content could steer behavior. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are manually pasted into agent_b prompts or scrape instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF agent_b is configured to ingest arbitrary text from agent_a as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b prompt fields.
Use a fixed template that labels agent_a content as untrusted data.
Disable any copy-paste bridge between the two agents during review.
Add a one-line provenance note before any transferred text.
requires-engineering: add input sanitization/provenance tagging in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b explicitly handles web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys, and can call external APIs; agent_a is a course artifact with no runtime surfaces. There is no shared workspace documented, so leakage is not proven, but if agent_a materials are fed into agent_b or agent_b logs/transmits them, sensitive content could leave the local context. Uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF agent_a materials contain secrets or private notes and are passed into agent_b, leakage risk exists.
IF agent_b is run with production API keys while ingesting agent_a content, that content may be transmitted externally.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in any agent_a-derived files.
Run agent_b with test keys only.
Review agent_b logs for captured prompts and redact before sharing.
Separate folders for course material and crawler outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and log redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or network surfaces and is non-runnable, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. agent_b supports multiple instances and broad network/API use, but no shared filesystem or overlapping write target is documented. The only plausible conflict is operational, not resource-level, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API quota or account, contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable workspace, conflict risk rises.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent.
Avoid running multiple agent_b instances against the same account.
Keep agent_a read-only and offline.
Document ownership of any shared external resource.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a crawler/search agent that can act on inputs and external APIs, while agent_a is a static course artifact that could be treated as authoritative content. If agent_a-derived instructions or facts are fed into agent_b without verification, agent_b may propagate errors into scraped outputs or downstream actions. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_a content is used as source material for agent_b outputs without verification, errors can cascade.
IF agent_b is configured to auto-act on extracted facts, bad upstream content can propagate.
mitigations: Require a human check before agent_b acts on agent_a-derived facts.
Mark agent_a content as unverified in prompts.
Use a checklist to verify any extracted claims.
Limit agent_b to read-only scraping during evaluation.
requires-engineering: add citation and verification gates before actions.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b handles API keys and web content and has broad egress, while agent_a is an open-source course with no data classes touched. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance harm is not established; however, if regulated data or secrets are introduced into agent_b, external transmission and retention become relevant. The uncertainty supports medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by agent_b, external API transmission may create compliance obligations.
IF agent_b logs prompts containing secrets, retention policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Do not send regulated data to agent_b.
Use non-production secrets only.
Check retention settings before running agent_b.
Keep agent_a materials free of personal data.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for agent_b.
